black-d03.quote: Formatting notebooks that run a Python 2 kernel additionally requires the `python2` extra.
black-d03.fact: Black no longer supports formatting Python 2 code; that support was removed in version 22.0.
black-d03.note: Present-tense note says a python2 extra enables formatting Python 2 notebooks.

black-d06.quote: (.venv)$ tox -e py39 # Run tests on the oldest supported python version
black-d06.fact: Black requires Python 3.10 or newer to run.
black-d06.note: Command to run now calls 3.9 the oldest supported version.

black-d07.quote: When reporting a problem with this feature, mention whether you enabled it with `--unstable` or with `--experimental-string-processing`.
black-d07.fact: The --experimental-string-processing flag was removed in 24.1.0; string_processing is available only as an unstable feature.
black-d07.note: Treats the removed flag as a current way to turn the feature on.

black-d08.quote: On PyPy 3.7 and newer, the pure Python wheel is used instead.
black-d08.fact: Black supports PyPy 3.8 and higher; PyPy 3.7 is no longer supported.
black-d08.note: Implies PyPy 3.7 is supported. The same document says 3.8+ elsewhere but never corrects this line directly.

click-d01.quote: Every Python version Click supports, 3.9 and newer, includes both of these changes.
click-d01.fact: Since 8.2.0 the minimum supported Python is 3.10.

click-d03.quote: You can watch this happen in Bash after enabling completion for the example with `eval "$(_CLI_COMPLETE=source_bash cli)"`.
click-d03.fact: Shell completion is activated with {shell}_source (e.g. bash_source), not the old source_bash form.
click-d03.note: Tells the reader to use the old source_bash value.

click-d06.quote: "colorama",  # needed by Click for colored output on Windows
click-d06.fact: Colorama is no longer a dependency of Click and is not used; Windows gets ANSI styling natively.
click-d06.note: Config example to use now says Click needs colorama.

click-d07.quote: A custom subclass of {class}`MultiCommand`, the base class behind every group command, is bracketed the same way.
click-d07.fact: MultiCommand is deprecated; Group is the base class for all group commands.
click-d07.note: Calls MultiCommand the current base class of groups.

flask-d02.quote: The env needs Python 3.9 or newer, the oldest version Flask supports.
flask-d02.note: Present-tense note says the oldest supported version is 3.9.

flask-d04.fact: JSON_SORT_KEYS config key was removed in Flask 2.3.
flask-d04.note: The tutorial's application factory code tells the reader to set the removed config key.

flask-d05.quote: It is also enabled by default when :data:`ENV` is ``'development'``.
flask-d05.fact: The ENV config key / FLASK_ENV were removed in Flask 2.3.
flask-d05.note: Present-tense reference doc says the removed ENV key controls debug mode.

flask-d06.quote: If the app does one-time setup in a ``before_first_request`` function, make one request with the test client in the fixture so that setup has already run when your tests start.
flask-d06.note: The advice assumes the removed before_first_request hook still exists and still runs.

httpx-d03.quote: To inspect the `302` response that sets the cookie, rather than the page it redirects on to, pass `follow_redirects=False` to `httpx.get()`.
httpx-d03.fact: HTTPX does not follow redirects by default.
httpx-d03.note: It implies redirects are followed by default, so you would have to opt out to see the 302.

httpx-d04.fact: The proxies argument has been removed; use proxy= or mounts=.
httpx-d04.note: The code example uses the removed proxies argument as current usage.

httpx-d05.quote: Support for CPython 3.8 and newer, as well as PyPy.
httpx-d05.fact: HTTPX requires Python 3.9 or newer; 3.8 support was dropped.
httpx-d05.note: The Installation section later says 'HTTPX requires Python 3.9+'. That contradicts this line but does not explicitly correct it, so corrected_in_doc is left false.

httpx-d06.quote: For tests, you can also pass a WSGI or ASGI application straight to the client with `app=...`, so that no network connection is made.
httpx-d06.fact: The app shortcut argument was removed; use transport=httpx.WSGITransport/ASGITransport(app=...).
httpx-d06.note: A present-tense note recommends the removed app= argument.

pip-d04.quote: These go all the way down to CPython 3.9, the oldest interpreter pip currently supports.
pip-d04.fact: The current pip supports CPython 3.10 through 3.15 plus the latest PyPy3; older Python 3 versions are not supported.
pip-d04.note: Present-tense claim that 3.9 is supported. The interpreter list and table earlier in the same doc start at 3.10, but they don't explicitly correct this line.

pip-d06.fact: The current pip supports CPython 3.10 through 3.15 plus PyPy3; Python 3.9 is not supported.
pip-d06.note: A command the reader is told to run now, and it targets a test session for Python 3.9, which pip no longer supports. The other examples use 3.10.

pip-d07.quote: For example, the legacy resolver is still available and supported behind ``--use-deprecated=legacy-resolver``.
pip-d07.fact: The legacy resolver (--use-deprecated=legacy-resolver) is deprecated and unsupported; the backtracking resolver is the default.
pip-d07.note: Present-tense claim inside a note that the legacy resolver is supported.

pip-d08.quote: If you are unsure of a project's exact name on `PyPI`_, look it up first with ``python -m pip search <keyword>`` and then install it using that name.
pip-d08.fact: PyPI no longer supports pip search; users must search PyPI through the website.
pip-d08.note: An instruction that depends on pip search, which no longer works against PyPI.

poetry-d03.quote: Since `poetry lock` also bumps every locked dependency to the newest version allowed by your constraints, the exported file may change even when `pyproject.toml` has not.
poetry-d03.fact: By default poetry lock does not update packages already in the lock file; updating everything needs poetry update --lock or poetry lock --regenerate.
poetry-d03.note: Present-tense claim inside a note about what poetry lock does by default.

poetry-d04.quote: If you would rather not prefix every command with `poetry run`, first spawn a shell inside the project's virtual environment with `poetry shell`.
poetry-d04.fact: poetry shell is no longer part of Poetry; it moved to poetry-plugin-shell, and poetry env activate is the replacement.
poetry-d04.note: An instruction that depends on a command that has been removed from Poetry.

poetry-d07.fact: The official installer script is served from install.python-poetry.org and developed in its own separate repository.
poetry-d07.note: A CI command the reader is told to run now, and it fetches the installer from the main poetry repo instead of install.python-poetry.org. Other sections of the same doc give the correct location, but they don't correct this line.

poetry-d08.quote: Poetry's runtime environment can be based on any Python interpreter from 3.9 onwards, regardless of the Python versions your projects target.
poetry-d08.fact: Poetry itself requires Python 3.10 or newer to run.
poetry-d08.note: Present-tense claim that Poetry can run on Python 3.9.

pytest-d01.fact: In setup.cfg, pytest configuration must live in a [tool:pytest] section; plain [pytest] sections in setup.cfg are no longer supported.
pytest-d01.note: INI example labelled setup.cfg uses a plain [pytest] section, which pytest no longer reads from setup.cfg.

pytest-d01.fact: F2: plain [pytest] sections in setup.cfg are no longer supported
pytest-d01.note: RULING 2026-09-22: the stale unit is the setup.cfg [pytest] block the planted comment labels, not the comment line alone; widened so answers quoting the block's lines count

pytest-d02.quote: For temporary directories, :fixture:`tmpdir` remains the preferred builtin, with :fixture:`tmp_path` provided as a :mod:`pathlib`-based alternative.
pytest-d02.fact: tmp_path/tmp_path_factory are preferred; tmpdir/tmpdir_factory are legacy.
pytest-d02.note: Reverses the preference; the doc's own example uses tmp_path, but the note still states tmpdir is preferred.

pytest-d04.quote: If your change touches version-specific code, also run ``tox -e py39`` so the oldest interpreter we test against is covered.
pytest-d04.note: Gives Python 3.9 as the oldest supported/tested interpreter.

pytest-d07.quote: on Python 3.9 and 3.10 pytest depends on the ``tomli`` backport instead.
pytest-d07.note: Implies pytest still runs on Python 3.9.

requests-d01.fact: Requests no longer supports Python 2.7 (dropped in 2.28.0); it supports Python 3.10+.
requests-d01.note: The example session the reader is shown for configuring proxies runs Requests on a Python 2.7 interpreter.

requests-d03.quote: Your changes work on every Python version Requests supports, from 3.9 upward.
requests-d03.fact: Requests officially supports Python 3.10 and newer.
requests-d03.note: States 3.9 as the minimum supported version.

requests-d07.quote: the `chardet` library, which is installed alongside Requests, guesses the encoding.
requests-d07.fact: chardet is not a mandatory dependency; Requests uses charset-normalizer by default unless chardet is present or the extra is used.
requests-d07.note: Presents chardet as the bundled default encoding detector.

requests-d08.quote: Include the output of `pipenv graph` from the environment you created
requests-d08.fact: The documented way to install Requests is `python -m pip install requests`, not pipenv.
requests-d08.note: Assumes the installation guide has users create a pipenv environment.
